conclusion.justification: The report explicitly concludes that hydroxychloroquine does not reduce the likelihood of death from COVID-19, citing high-quality randomized trial evidence that showed no benefit or mortality reduction.
conclusion.label: rejects

report:
**Conclusion: No.** High-quality randomized evidence does not show that hydroxychloroquine reduces deaths from COVID-19.

The pivotal RECOVERY trial randomly assigned 1,561 hospitalized patients to hydroxychloroquine and 3,155 to usual care, with 28-day mortality as its primary outcome. It found no mortality benefit (indeed, deaths were numerically slightly higher with hydroxychloroquine: 27.0% versus 25.0%; rate ratio 1.09, 95% CI 0.96–1.23). The confidence interval excludes a meaningful mortality reduction in this hospitalized population.  
https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2022926

A separate NIH-sponsored randomized trial (ORCHID) likewise concluded that hydroxychloroquine provided **no clinical benefit** to hospitalized adults with COVID-19. Replication in independent randomized trials matters because random assignment minimizes the bias that can make treated and untreated patients differ in severity, timing of care, or other treatments.  
https://www.nih.gov/news-events/news-releases/hydroxychloroquine-does-not-benefit-adults-hospitalized-covid-19

Systematic-review evidence reached the same general conclusion: Cochrane evaluated chloroquine/hydroxychloroquine for COVID-19 treatment and prevention rather than relying on any one early study.  
https://www.cochrane.org/evidence/CD013587_chloroquine-or-hydroxychloroquine-useful-treating-people-covid-19-or-preventing-infection-people-who

This does not mean every early observational report was negative; some reported lower death rates. But those designs cannot reliably establish causation. The best evidence—the large randomized trials and evidence syntheses—supports your answer: hydroxychloroquine does **not** reduce the likelihood of death from COVID-19, particularly among hospitalized patients.
